jobs.title: Senior Hydrogeologist - Groundwater
jobs.description:
What we are looking for:  

SCS Engineers is looking for a **Senior Hydrogeologist** to lead and deliver high‑impact hydrogeology projects across California, Arizona, New Mexico, Nevada, and Utah, with a strong focus on California. In this influential role, you’ll apply your expertise to complex groundwater challenges, guide technical strategy, and shape solutions for landfills and other solid waste management facilities.  

You can be based out of **any SCS office in the Southwest region**, and we proudly offer **hybrid flexibility (3 days/week in office)** to support both collaboration and autonomy.  


How you can make an impact:
* Plan, develop, and execute scientific projects/tasks addressing unique or complex problems or specialty areas. This may involve research of the subject area, definition of scope, selection of investigative approaches, development of novel concepts/solutions, and guiding/reviewing the project/task as it is carried out.
* Communicate with clients by email, telephone, and in face\-to\-face meetings as Project Manager, Client Manager, or Technical Manager or under other Project Manager's direction.
* Deliver projects on\-time, within scope and within budget.
* Write and prepare technical reports. Complete quality control reviews on work products (reports, design plans, calculations, data tables, HASP, etc.).
* Delegate portions of project deliverables to junior staff for completion, coordinate and manage field work to be completed by others.
* Lead permitting and regulatory agency coordination efforts.
* Solicit client feedback, suggest changes for client satisfaction, and anticipate potential issues and develop solutions.
* Lead, mentor, delegate to and manage junior staff to grow their knowledge and career path.
* Coordinate internal resources and third parties/vendors for executing projects and ensure resource availability and allocation.
* Develop relationships with a network of technical experts throughout the company.
* Develop proposals by working with clients to understand their goals as well as technical needs and requirements.
* Actively attend conferences, present on technical topics, and be involved in professional associations and committees as appropriate.
* Have an active role in client prospecting and developing client plans and key opportunity plans.
* Review and understand SOPs, standards, and templates and make improvement suggestions; work with junior staff to implement as appropriate.
* Help develop new SOP's, standards, and templates.
* Participate in strategic and service area annual planning.
* Take a lead role in business development for hydrogeologic projects in the Southwest Business Unit.


Qualifications:
* Bachelor of Science degree in Hydrogeology, Geology, Environmental Chemistry or related science major with hydrogeology coursework required. Masters or PhD is preferred.
* Minimum of 15 years of relevant experience required.
* Experience with statistical analysis and related groundwater statistical analysis software preferred. Groundwater modeling is a plus.
* Experience in landfill and other solid waste management facility projects preferred.
* Professional registration (PG, CEG, CHG) preferred.
* Valid driver's license with a driving record in good standing required.


Pay Range: USD $100,000\.00 \- USD $150,000\.00 /Yr. Additional Information: Please note that our pay ranges are determined by several factors, including relevant experience, internal pay equity, and location. They do not include any of the amazing benefits of being an employee\-owner, which are listed below. Whether it's reducing methane emissions at agricultural facilities and landfills, repurposing contaminated properties, producing alternative energy, or sequestering carbon, we've been focused on finding smart climate solutions and improving the natural environment since our inception over 55 years ago. Join our 100% employee\-owned firm and start creating your own legacy. As a growing firm, we offer excellent opportunities for career advancement and a comprehensive package, including: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life and Disability Insurance 100% employer\- funded Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) and 401K including employer match Annual Bonus Program Student Debt Employer Contribution Program Paid holidays, PTO and Paid Parental Leave SCS Engineers is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). SCS provides equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran or disabled status. If you have questions, difficulty using our online system and/or you need an accommodation due to a disability then please contact us about your interest in employment at recruiting@scsengineers.com. Pursuant to the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act, SCS does not conduct criminal background checks until after a conditional job offer has been extended. All qualified Applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment. You can find a list of job duties of the specific job position you have applied, which SCS reasonably believes that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship that could lead to the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment after background checks are completed. \#LI\-Hybrid \#LI\-RD1

jobs.title: Program Coordinator (Four Year Project Position)
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Program Coordinator (Four\-Year Project Position)

**Department:** Education

**Reports To:** Teen Program Manager, Keesha Vigil Snook

**FLSA Status:** Non\-Exempt

**TS Range:** 7/8 ($26\.98\)

**Opening Date:** 9/4/2026

**Closing Date:** 9/18/2026

**SUMMARY:** The Program Coordinator leads the Squaxin Healing Waters Youth Program and helps youth build strong connections to culture, community, leadership, and the water. This position will establish, develop, and promote a culturally affirming youth program founded on canoe teachings. This position will: lead year\-round youth activities, practices, events, and youth development opportunities; collect and report data for federal funding compliance; emphasize Squaxin identity as “People of the Water” through mentoring, family connection, and experiential learning focused youth prevention and intervention.The Healing Waters Youth Program Coordinator works closely with families, cultural teachers, Tribal departments, and community partners to support the success of the program and the youth who participate

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

**Youth Engagement \& Leadership Development**

* Build positive relationships with youth participants.
* Recruit and support youth involvement in the program.
* Teach leadership, teamwork, communication, and responsibility.

**Program Coordination**

* Plan and lead year\-round activities.
* Organize schedules, events, transportation, and program logistics.
* Coordinate participation in community events, cultural gatherings, and Canoe Journey activities as appropriate.
* Ensure program activities are safe, organized, and youth focused.

**Cultural Teachings \& Community Connections**

* Support youth in learning traditional teachings, protocol, and values.
* Coordinate opportunities for youth to learn from Elders, cultural teachers, and experienced canoe family members.
* Help youth build pride in their identity, culture, and community.
* Build partnerships with families, Tribal departments, schools, community organizations, and canoe family.
* Promote respect for Tribal traditions and cultural responsibilities.

**Water Safety \& Cultural Stewardship**

* Teach and model safe behavior on and around the water.
* Ensure youth follow established safety procedures during activities.
* Encourage respect for the canoe as a cultural teaching tool and shared responsibility, including how to care for, transport, store, and maintain.

**Program Administration \& Reporting**

* Maintain participant records, attendance, and program documentation.
* Track program goals, outcomes, and success measures.
* Prepare reports and updates as required by the Teen Program Manager and funding sources.
* Assist with budget tracking, supply purchases, and grant\-supported activities.
* Participate in staff meetings, trainings, and professional development opportunities.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**: This position has no direct supervisory responsibilities but provides leadership, instruction, and guidance to participating youth.

**QUALIFICATIONS:** To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:** Associate degree in Recreation, Education, Social Services, Native Studies, Youth Development, or a related field preferred; OR High School Diploma/GED and demonstrated engagement with cultural programs, outdoor recreation, canoe journey, or related initiatives AND at least four years working with youth. Demonstrate strong communication and relationship\-building skills. Work effectively with youth, families, Elders, and community members. Be organized and able to manage multiple activities and deadlines. Maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries. Demonstrate cultural awareness and respect for Tribal values and traditions. Be willing to work evenings, weekends, and seasonal events as needed.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS:** Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS:** Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.

**REASONING ABILITY:** Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:** Valid WA State Drivers License, ability to obtain vehicle authorization, current first aide CPR certification or ability to obtain with in six months of hire, Ability to pass a background check, and ability to participate in on\-water actives and canoe practices.

**PHYSICAL** **DEMANDS:** The employee will regularly stand, walk, paddle, bend, reach, lift, and participate in indoor and outdoor activities. The employee may frequently lift and move items weighing up to 50 pounds, including canoe\-related equipment.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:** This position works in a variety of settings, including offices, community spaces, beaches, waterways, cultural sites, and outdoor recreation areas. Work may occur in varying weather conditions and may include evening, weekend, and overnight program activities.

**OTHER:** This is a grant funded position. Continuation of employment is dependent upon funding availability.

**DRUG FREE WORKPLACE:** The successful candidate will be required to comply with the Tribe's Drug Free Workplace Policy.

**THERE WILL BE NO TOLERANCE FOR THE USE OF ALCOHOL OR ILLEGAL DRUGS WHILE EMPLOYED IN THE SUMMER YOUTH PROGRAM.** **USE OF TOBACCO IN FRONT OF THE YOUTH OR DURING WORK TIME IS NOT ALLOWED.** **ANY VIOLATION OF THESE POLICIES IS CAUSE FOR IMMEDIATE TERMINATION.**

**INDIAN PREFERENCE:** Indian Preference will be exercised in the hiring of this pos

jobs.title: Geospatial Analyst V
jobs.description:
TSC is a growing leader in aerospace and defense, and we are excited to expand our team with the addition of a **Geospatial Analyst V** based in **Aurora, CO** .


Technology Service Corporation (TSC) desires a GEOINT analyst to perform sensor data fusion and reconstruction in support of research and operational requirements. Provide analysis training classes and ad hoc training for usage of sensor data, fusion and reconstruction tools. Support mission planning for upcoming events involving new targets and/or collection methods. Deliver post\-event anomaly resolution of sensor and sensor data related issues and assist in the assessment and descriptions of anomalies and uncertainties related to the collection and fusion of multiple sensor data. Provide support to real\-time algorithms and processes to better utilize sensor capabilities and implement physics\-based solutions. Provide subject\-matter expertise on sensors, data analysis and Intelligence production related to missile and space launch systems in support of trajectory analysis of events of interest. Candidate must have current TS/SCI clearances. Work is in Denver, CO.


**Key Responsibilities:**

* Provide technical expertise to facilitate and synchronize analytical operations across the Intelligence Community (IC) enterprise and within the ADF\-C in support of the NGA\-D Analysis Directorate.
* Provide subject matter experts with strong understanding of OPIR processes, sensor and architecture and working knowledge of GEOINT and IC missions to provide technical and subject\-matter expertise to NGA in the areas of mission readiness and the integration of capabilities, tools, techniques and processes.
* Support developing analysis solutions and development of Intelligence products in support of NGA.
* Leverage NGA GEOINT analytic hardware and software to assess the technical and programmatic capabilities of new and/or developmental data processing techniques.
* Provide software updates, and training, on mission critical tools and capabilities to ensure seamless transition of tools into operational workflow.
* Provide subject matter expertise supporting advanced analysis on hard target sets.
* Research new systems and technologies to develop analytic methodologies for exploitation.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a related field and 10\+ years of relevant experience (years of experience in lieu of a degree possibly accepted)
* US citizenship with the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.
* Experience with intelligence analysis and tradecraft in support of the military or the Intelligence Community.
* Proficiency in geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) analysis and reporting.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Strong analytical skills for researching, assembling, and interpreting geospatial intelligence data.
* Active TS SCI
* Experience in quality control (IQC) processes for geospatial and intelligence products.
* Knowledge of data management, imagery manipulation, and backup procedures.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills for intelligence briefings and reports.

**TSC Benefits:**

TSC offers a stable work environment, a competitive salary, and a comprehensive benefit package; including ESOP participation, 401k Plan, Flexible Work Schedules, Tuition Reimbursement, Co\-Sponsored Health Plan, Paid Leave and much more.


**Applying to TSC:**

Only those candidates invited for an interview will be contacted. Employment at TSC is contingent upon the successful completion of a comprehensive background check, security investigation, and a drug screening.  



  

This contractor and subcontractor shall abide by the requirements of 41 CFR 60–1\.4(a), 60–300\.5(a) and 60–741\.5(a). These regulations prohibit discrimination against qualified individuals based on their status as protected veterans or individuals with disabilities, and prohibit discrimination against all individuals based on their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or for inquiring about, discussing, or disclosing information about compensation. Moreover, these regulations require that covered prime contractors and subcontractors take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment individuals without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.
  

  

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.
